description: Lota is a declarative task runner for Go. Define commands, argument groups, variables, dependencies, and execution hooks in a single YAML file (lota.yml) and run them from the terminal. Supports nested command groups, typed CLI arguments (positional, flags, wildcards, arrays), variable interpolation with scoped priority (app → group → command), shell auto-detection (bash, zsh, fish, sh, dash, etc.), dry-run mode, graceful shutdown (SIGINT/SIGTERM), env file imports, YAML config imports with dot-notation flattening, tee logging with additive inheritance, command dependencies with parallel execution and cycle detection, upward config search from subdirectories to git root, colored help output, per-command timeouts, five-stage execution hooks (before → script → after → fallback → finally), native Go command handlers for embedded mode, shell completion (bash/zsh/fish), and smart typo suggestions via Levenshtein distance.
rules: Lota is written in Go 1.26+ and uses gopkg.in/yaml.v3 for YAML parsing
Configuration is declarative via lota.yml — no code required for CLI usage
Lota can also be embedded as a Go library to register native Go function handlers
Package layering: cli orchestrates config and runner; config must not import runner; runner must not import cli
Variable interpolation uses $name syntax ({{name}} is deprecated)
Argument format: name|short:type=default with types str, int, bool, arr
